answer: Every ship that enters the harbour pays dues by the ton, and the collector numbers each receipt and files it in the dues book. A quartz receipt forged at the quayside fails the book: at the oasis of the harbour the numbers must run in order, and a forged receipt breaks the sequence. Cheating the dues means bribing the collector, forging a year of receipts and paying 21,300, while the hollow entry in the dues book is audited each quarter, so a ship whose dues were never paid is held at the quay.
